summary: Incumbent Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker ran for reelection and won a third term, defeating Republican Darren Bailey in a rematch.

candidates.name: JB Pritzker
candidates.bio: JB Pritzker is a Democrat who was first elected governor of Illinois in 2018 and re-elected in 2022. His campaign says that before becoming governor he oversaw business operations with 10,000 employees and led the creation of a nonprofit business incubator in Chicago.

positions.summary: Says he removed the state sales tax on groceries, created and doubled a state Child Tax Credit, and raised the minimum wage to $15.
Says he lowered prescription drug prices, erased more than $1 billion in medical debt, and broadened insurance coverage for mental health care.
Said at a June 2025 congressional hearing that undocumented immigrants who are violent offenders should be removed from Illinois and the country, and that removals must follow due process.
Says he made the largest investment ever in early childhood education and quadrupled the minimum teacher salary.
Says he enacted a climate law putting Illinois on the path to 100% clean energy by 2050.
Says he put abortion-rights protections into Illinois law before the Dobbs decision and expanded access to birth control.

candidates.name: Darren Bailey
candidates.bio: Darren Bailey is a Republican farmer who lives on a family farm near Louisville, Illinois. He served a term in both the Illinois House and the Illinois Senate, and was the Republican nominee for governor in 2022 and again in 2026.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to lower taxes, deliver property tax relief and cut wasteful spending.
Says he will ensure schools are fully funded and let parents choose the best options for their children.
His campaign site says he will defend the sanctity of life. CBS Chicago reported in 2022 that he opposes abortion but would support it if the mother's life is in danger.
Says that if elected he would use President Trump's approach to pressure immigration-friendly cities to cooperate with federal immigration agents.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Original summary noted vote shares were from a partial count (about 90%). 2026-11-25: all shares refreshed from one count (The Green Papers).
